source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

rate_sensitive.evidence: FY25 highlights cited by search sources note Lupin reached zero net debt with margin gains and a dividend hike, suggesting minimal floating-rate liability exposure, but no explicit % disclosed in accessible sources.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Lupin operates in 100+ markets and is exposed to USD-INR, EUR-INR and ZAR-INR fluctuations; uses natural hedges and forex derivatives (forward contracts), with treasury operations adopting layered hedging strategies.
inr_exposure.evidence: Operating in 100+ markets exposes Lupin to currency fluctuations, particularly USD-INR, EUR-INR, and ZAR-INR. While natural hedges and forex derivatives are deployed, extreme currency movements can impact profitability. Lupin's treasury operations actively monitor exposures and adopt layered hedging strategies.

pli_scheme.evidence: Lupin holds PLI-scheme approval for bulk drugs/APIs (KSMs) tied to its Vizag/Tarapur API manufacturing facilities under India's PLI Scheme for critical bulk drugs; specific revenue/incentive percentage not confirmed from primary source within research budget.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/broker commentary characterizes Divi's Labs as a primary beneficiary of the China+1 strategy in the CDMO/API space, as global pharma companies diversify supply chains away from China. Could not directly access the FY24-25 AR MD&A to confirm exact company wording; widely repeated third-party framing, not a verified direct quote.

crude_exposure.evidence: Secondary-source commentary: concentrated sourcing risk for methanol, imported solvents and Middle-East-sourced crude derivatives; raw material prices inflated due to energy crisis; no exact % found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: No explicit forward-contract hedge ratio located; uses long-term customer contracts with price-adjustment mechanisms rather than a disclosed fixed hedge ratio.
inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (predominantly USD/EUR-invoiced) were ~87-89% of gross sales across FY23-FY26 per broker/rating-agency summaries.

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's has announced PLI-supported capacity expansions in API segments (fermentation-based APIs, backward integration) where Chinese pricing had previously made domestic investment unviable; exact revenue % not found.

china_plus_one.evidence: FY25 base-business revenue split: USA ~72%, Europe ~4%, Canada/Australia/NZ ~3%, India ~6%, Rest of World ~15% shows heavy export concentration, but no accessible Gland Pharma source contained an explicit company self-description as a China+1 beneficiary.

pli_scheme.evidence: Gland Pharma not named among identified PLI pharma/API scheme beneficiaries in available sources; no disclosure of PLI participation found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary news snippet on FY25 results (not primary AR text): Indian makers of APIs seeing rising demand in key European and U.S. markets and expected to benefit further as global drugmakers diversify supply chains away from China. Could not confirm if Alivus own MD&A uses explicit China+1 framing since AR PDF was unreachable (403).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company reported healthy FY25 cash flows and a debt-free balance sheet per secondary source, suggesting minimal rate exposure; no borrowings note accessible to confirm.

pli_scheme.evidence: Secondary analyst-note snippet references FY25 EBITDA margins declining slightly versus FY24 despite the absence of PLI benefit in the current year, indicating Alivus received a PLI (bulk drugs/API) benefit in FY23-24 that lapsed in FY24-25. No revenue % or amount found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Offshore/international business (NAM Singapore offshore managed mandates, international advisory mandates, and new GIFT City IFSC branch) reportedly contributed approximately 5% of NAM-INDIA total revenue in FY25, with offshore AUM growing ~56% YoY. Figures derived from secondary aggregation of investor-presentation/earnings-call commentary.

rural.evidence: Ginger (IHCL midscale brand) growth is concentrated in emerging leisure and pilgrimage markets in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities per secondary source (Skift/Business Standard coverage), not verified against primary AR text.

inr_exposure.evidence: Earnings-call commentary noted international headwinds post West Asia conflict causing an estimated INR 40-50 crore revenue loss on consolidated basis including the London hotel, indicating some foreign-currency/international revenue exposure, but no explicit USD revenue % or hedging policy found.

rural.evidence: Secondary press commentary references management discussing tier-2 cities and white spirits driving next demand phase, but no quantified rural/semi-urban revenue % found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Total debt ~INR 1,000 crore, short-term borrowings ~INR 693 crore as of Mar-2025 per secondary source, but no floating-vs-fixed-rate split located.

crude_exposure.evidence: Secondary brokerage commentary noted packaging cost inflation (glass bottles, cartons) linked to rising crude oil prices and a weaker rupee raising import costs for packaging inputs; no raw-material % figure verified against AR.

inr_exposure.evidence: Secondary sources indicate exports contribute roughly 9-10% of revenue across 85-100+ countries; not independently verified against AR text.

rural.evidence: FY2023-24 AR reportedly stated Metro and Tier-1 cities contribute more than 50% of revenue, implying Tier-2/3/4 and rural markets combined make up the remainder; exact rural-only percentage not found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Third-party analysis of Mankind Pharma FY23 AR stated the company had not reported use of any formal FX hedging tools/techniques, in contrast to peers like Sun Pharma, Cipla, Dr Reddy's which use forwards/swaps/options.
inr_exposure.evidence: Mankind Pharma dealt in various currencies but the company had not reported the use of any tool or technique to manage FX risk in their annual report for FY23.

pli_scheme.evidence: No disclosure found indicating Mankind Pharma participates in the PLI scheme for bulk drugs/APIs; company is predominantly a branded-formulations/consumer-healthcare business rather than a bulk API manufacturer targeted by that scheme.

rural.evidence: Revenue share from developing hospitals (Lucknow and Patna) increased from 23.4% to 28.9% of total revenue in Q1 FY25 per company investor disclosure (quarterly figure, not full-year FY25).

govt_capex.evidence: Medanta is empanelled under Ayushman Bharat, CGHS and ECHS government health schemes; management disclosed scheme-specific receivable/credit-period data but no revenue % contribution from these schemes was found disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Revenue from international patients increased ~8% YoY to INR 2,086 million in FY25, contributing approximately 6% of total revenue (figure repeated consistently across Q3 FY25 and Q4 FY25 disclosures).

rate_sensitive.evidence: FY25 average cost of debt declined to ~8.5% from ~9.2% in FY24; gross debt ~INR 4,400 crore with Net Debt/EBITDA of 1.2x. Management commentary noted new asset-level debt is being raised primarily via Lease Rental Discounting (LRD), typically priced at floating/repo-linked rates. Exact floating-vs-fixed split from AR notes to accounts not retrieved.

china_plus_one.evidence: FY25 total revenue INR 4,784 crore (up 16% YoY); Export Formulations ~INR 3,760 crore (~78.6% of revenue), growth driven by higher gRevlimid sales in the US and export formulations growth in Brazil/Canada subsidiaries. No explicit China+1/supply-chain-diversification framing tied to revenue growth found; exports dominant but without explicit diversification-away-from-China language.

pli_scheme.evidence: Natco Pharma reported as approved under Group B of India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (bulk drugs/KSMs/APIs), aimed at boosting domestic API/KSM manufacturing and reducing import dependence on China. No revenue % attributable to PLI-linked production disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company appears to hedge a portion of USD-denominated revenue/cash flows against INR cost base; an analyst note referenced an INR ~90 million hedging loss factored into a quarterly revenue line item, implying an active forex hedging program, though full hedging policy details not accessible.
inr_exposure.evidence: Nearly 96% of IKS Health's revenue derived from the US market (India/domestic ~4% or less).

rural.evidence: FY25 commentary indicates Tier-2 and Tier-3 geographies growing faster than Tier-1 for Nykaa; ~70% of beauty orders still come from India's top 110 cities (implying ~30% from beyond); B2B House of Nykaa Superstore platform derives ~88% of GMV from Tier-2 cities. No single consolidated revenue percentage from rural/Tier-2-3 markets disclosed for FY25 group.

china_plus_one.evidence: As global supply chains continue to diversify, our strong alignment with India's industrial growth becomes increasingly evident. Amid geopolitical instability and global trade restrictions the Company diversified sourcing and logistics strategies, established alternative shipping routes; North America alone contributing ~41% of revenue with expansion to Western markets described as strategic geographic diversification.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Consolidated interest rate risk note: Variable rate borrowings INR 134.63mn, Fixed rate borrowings nil (Total borrowings INR 134.63mn) as at 31 March 2025; FY24: Variable INR 2,330.58mn, Fixed nil. Total borrowings very small relative to revenue (~INR 3,555 crore).

crude_exposure.evidence: Company consumes alloy steel, steel, aluminium and copper as major commodities; majority of commodity price risk is a passthrough via customer contracts, so no specific commodity hedging undertaken. Material cost accounted for 43% of total income in FY2024-25 and FY2023-24. No crude-oil linkage disclosed; steel/metal alloys are the primary inputs.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Board-approved hedging policy primarily employs forward contracts to hedge currency risk (primarily USD and EUR exposure from sales in USA, Europe, China and purchases from overseas suppliers).
inr_exposure.evidence: Company operates internationally, and a large portion of the business is transacted in international currencies primarily US$ and EUR, exposed to foreign exchange risk through sales and services in the USA, Europe, China and other countries.

pli_scheme.evidence: Benefited from income accrual from the Auto PLI scheme, for which eight products were approved.
